channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Russia Strikes Kyiv Bridges in Massive Overnight Attack Hours After Summit With Trump and Xi
item.description: Russia launched a massive overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine hours after President Vladimir Putin left Shenzhen, killing at least five people and damaging three bridges across the Dnipro River in Kyiv.

item.title: APEC Leaders Adopt Shenzhen Declaration, Pledging Closer Ties and Fewer Trade Barriers
item.description: Leaders of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum have adopted a joint declaration in Shenzhen pledging stronger regional connectivity and fewer barriers to trade and investment, closing their two-day summit in the southern Chinese city.

item.title: Gulf Shipping Insurance Soars as Blockade Squeezes Trade
item.description: A United States maritime agency memo says the naval blockade of Iran is pushing up insurance premiums and cutting cargo capacity in the Gulf, as the cost of sending ships through the Strait of Hormuz climbs sharply.

item.title: GTA 6 Smashes Records With an Estimated $2.36 Billion on Day One
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 has made an estimated $2.36 billion in its first day on sale, selling about 24.6 million copies and dwarfing the record set by its predecessor, according to market tracker Sensor Tower.

item.title: Thousands March Across Colombia Against Tax Rises and Closer US Military Ties
item.description: Thousands of people have marched through Bogota and other Colombian cities in a second nationwide protest against President Abelardo de la Espriella, opposing his tax plans and questioning closer military cooperation with the United States.

item.title: Fiona, the Internet-Famous Hippo, Dies at 9 After Swallowing a Visitor's Hat
item.description: Fiona, the hippopotamus whose fight for life as a premature calf made her famous around the world, has died at the Cincinnati Zoo at the age of nine, days after swallowing a knit hat that fell into her enclosure.

item.title: Trump's Election Security Pick Says Jan 6 Was Not an Attack at Senate Hearing
item.description: The nominee chosen to lead the agency that helps protect American elections told senators on Thursday that he does not believe the storming of the US Capitol on January 6, 2021 was an attack, and he refused to say who won the 2020 presidential election.

item.title: Meta Rethinks 2030 Net-Zero Goal as AI Data Centres Push Emissions Up 45%
item.description: Meta is reconsidering its pledge to reach net-zero emissions by 2030, the company said in its annual sustainability report on Thursday, blaming the surge in energy demand from its artificial intelligence build-out for pushing its carbon footprint sharply higher.

item.title: Kirkland & Ellis Gave $11.8m in Free Legal Work to Trump Administration, Democrats Say
item.description: The law firm Kirkland & Ellis has provided at least $11.8 million in free legal services to federal agencies since striking a deal with President Donald Trump's administration, three senior Democrats said on Thursday, calling the arrangement evidence of a corrupt bargain.

item.title: UK to Send Ukraine More Than 1,000 Long-Range Strike Drones in £260m Package
item.description: Britain will supply Ukraine with more than 1,000 long-range strike drones under a new £260 million military aid package, Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced on Thursday in Berlin, saying the weapons will let Kyiv strike military targets far behind the front line.

item.title: Haiti Police Say 34 Suspected Gang Members Killed in Martissant Raid
item.description: Haiti's national police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in a major operation on Thursday in Martissant, a southern district of the capital that has been under gang control for more than five years, and reported no officers or civilians hurt.

item.title: Iran-Linked Plot Suspect Declares Innocence and Seeks New Lawyers in New York Court
item.description: A dual Iranian-Iraqi national accused of directing a failed attack on a British airbase used by the United States military told a federal judge in New York on Thursday that he is innocent and no longer wants his court-appointed lawyers, in a hearing that ended with marshals escorting him from the courtroom.

item.title: Trump Posthumously Pardons Baseball Hit King Pete Rose
item.description: President Donald Trump has posthumously pardoned Pete Rose, baseball's all-time hits leader, more than two years after the star's death, clearing the tax convictions that followed his lifetime ban from the game.

item.title: Six Killed, Including Two Children, as Suspected Gas Blast Collapses Tbilisi Apartment Block
item.description: Six people, including two children, have been killed after a suspected gas explosion tore through part of a five-storey apartment building in Georgia's capital, Tbilisi, with a three-year-old girl pulled alive from the rubble after hours of rescue work.

item.title: California Subpoenas Nvidia Over Whether China Obtained Its Advanced Chips
item.description: California's attorney general has served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena, opening a formal inquiry into whether the chipmaker's actions allowed advanced chips or confidential information to reach China and whether investors were misled about the risk.

item.title: Appeals Court Keeps Venezuelan Deportation Protections Frozen for Now
item.description: A federal appeals court in San Francisco has kept deportation protections for hundreds of thousands of Venezuelans suspended, hours after the Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to intervene in the case.

item.title: Senate Rejects Bid to Rein In Trump's War Powers on Iran
item.description: The United States Senate has voted down a resolution that would have told the president to halt the fighting with Iran unless Congress approved it, in the chamber's first vote on the conflict since the midterm elections.

item.title: Burnham Says Europe Is Ready to Join Talks to End Russia's War in Ukraine
item.description: Britain's prime minister says Europe is ready to enter negotiations to end Russia's war in Ukraine, after a meeting of Kyiv's allies that also brought the American mediators trying to broker a settlement to the table.

item.title: Aid Group Warns Gaza's Children Face Dangers Seen Nowhere Else After Three Years of War
item.description: After three years of war, children in Gaza are living with dangers found nowhere else on Earth, Save the Children has warned in a new global report, with at least 20,000 children killed and survivors facing repeated displacement, hunger and the loss of schooling and health care.

item.title: Three French Officers Face Prison as Court Nears Verdict in 2020 Beating of Black Music Producer
item.description: A Paris court is due to deliver its verdict on Friday in the trial of three police officers accused of beating Black music producer Michel Zecler at his studio in November 2020, after prosecutors asked for prison terms of four to six years.

item.title: Anthropic Hits $2 Trillion in Record Nasdaq Debut
item.description: Anthropic's shares soared on their first day of trading on Thursday, pushing the maker of the Claude chatbot to a valuation of about $2 trillion in the biggest stock market debut ever recorded.

item.title: Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah Reach Deal as Federal Troops Prepare to Enter Militia Stronghold
item.description: Iraq's government has reached a compromise with the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah militia over control of its stronghold south of Baghdad, with federal troops due to move into the area on Friday morning under a joint command.

item.title: Trump Signals He Will Wait Until 2027 on Fresh Iran Strikes as War Cost Passes $48 Billion
item.description: President Donald Trump has signalled he is in no hurry to order a new round of strikes on Iran, saying he will decide after the new year, as the Pentagon put the cost of the war so far at more than $48 billion.

item.title: Putin Vows 'Far More Painful' Response After Third Strike on Crimean Bridge
item.description: President Vladimir Putin has vowed a response 'far more painful' than Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge, dropping any idea of a truce on energy and Black Sea attacks after the crossing was hit for a third time in a week.

item.title: European Commission Confirms AI-Tool Cyberattack Disrupted Its Systems for Over Ten Days
item.description: The European Commission has confirmed it was targeted by a cyber campaign carried out with the help of artificial intelligence tools, disrupting staff systems for more than ten days.

item.title: Pentagon Strategist Walked Out of NATO Meeting After Rebuking Ukraine Over Deep Strikes
item.description: The Pentagon's top policy official left a meeting with European allies in Brussels early after criticising Ukraine for its long-range strikes inside Russia, according to a report that has alarmed several allied governments.

item.title: Trump Official Suggested Venezuela Take Part of Guyana's Essequibo, Sources Say
item.description: A senior official in Donald Trump's administration raised the idea of Guyana handing Venezuela partial control of the Essequibo region, a vast territory that covers about two-thirds of Guyana, according to a report published on Thursday.

item.title: JPMorgan Chase Says Customer Names and Emails May Have Been Exposed in Vendor Cyberattack
item.description: JPMorgan Chase has said some customer names and email addresses may have been exposed after hackers attacked outside companies that provide services to the bank.

item.title: South Korea's Top Court Orders Retrial for Ex-PM Han Over Martial Law Role
item.description: South Korea's Supreme Court has overturned former prime minister Han Duck-soo's 15-year prison sentence over his role in the December 2024 martial law crisis and ordered a retrial, in the latest twist in the fallout from the six-hour decree.

item.title: Denmark Approves Greenland Security Deal With US in Unanimous Vote
item.description: Denmark's parliament has unanimously approved a security agreement with the United States covering Greenland, a deal meant to end months of tension over the Arctic island's future after repeated threats from Washington to take control of it.
